title: A Meteor Blew Up Over Russia With 30 Times the Power of Hiroshima

scenes.text: A meteor blew up over Russia with 30 times Hiroshima's power.
Twenty metres wide. 42,000 miles an hour. Nobody saw it coming.
It came out of the Sun's glare, and for a moment it was brighter than the Sun itself.
It burst 19 miles up. The shockwave arrived minutes later and shattered windows across six cities.
About 1,500 people were hurt, almost all by flying glass. Nobody was killed.
The biggest chunk was hauled from a lake. It broke the scale. 1,250 pounds.

description:
On February 15, 2013, a 20-metre asteroid exploded about 19 miles above Chelyabinsk, Russia, releasing roughly 500 kilotons of energy, about 30 times the Hiroshima bomb.
It entered at around 42,000 miles an hour from the direction of the Sun, so no telescope saw it coming. The flash briefly outshone the Sun, the shockwave damaged about 7,200 buildings in six cities and injured around 1,500 people, mostly from flying glass. The largest fragment, pulled from Lake Chebarkul, weighed about 1,250 pounds and broke the scale used to weigh it.
Where were you when you first saw the dashcam footage? Comment below.
first_comment: Most of the injuries happened because people ran to the windows to watch the flash, and the shockwave arrived a couple of minutes later. If you saw a flash brighter than the Sun, would you run to the window or away from it?
